translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, a provincial administration commission was established.

sentences.zh: 清初為浙江省，置巡撫，福建置總督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing it became Zhejiang Province; a governor-general was placed in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing it became Zhejiang Province, with a provincial governor appointed, while Fujian received a governor-general.

translations.literal: He also exercised jurisdiction over it.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general also exercised jurisdiction over Zhejiang.

translations.literal: Stationed at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The post was based at Fuzhou.

translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 (1658), a separate Zhejiang governor-general was created.

translations.literal: Stationed at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The office was first stationed at Wenzhou.

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi the seat was moved to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662) it was moved to Hangzhou.

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was abolished, and soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 (1669) the post was abolished, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 二十五年復裁，兼轄如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year it was again abolished; joint jurisdiction remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 (1686) it was abolished again, and Zhejiang reverted to the previous arrangement of joint jurisdiction from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，改巡撫為總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, the provincial governor was changed to governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 (1727), the provincial governor was elevated to governor-general.

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, it was again a provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 12 (1734), the office reverted to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，復置浙江總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, the Zhejiang governor-general was again established.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 (1736), the Zhejiang governor-general was restored.

sentences.zh: 三年，改閩浙總督，自是為定制。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was changed to the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general; from then on this became the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 (1738) the post was reorganized as the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general, which thereafter remained the standard arrangement.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，遣固山額真金礪來杭駐防，掌平南將軍印。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi, Gushan Ejin Jin Kan was sent to garrison Hangzhou and hold the seal of the Pacification of the South general.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 (1648), the banner general Jin Kan was dispatched to garrison Hangzhou, bearing the seal of the Pacification of the South general.

sentences.zh: 康熙初年改將軍，總督駐福州，將軍、巡撫駐杭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi the title was changed to general; the governor-general was stationed at Fuzhou, while the general and provincial governor were stationed at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi reign the post was retitled general; the governor-general remained at Fuzhou, while the general and provincial governor were stationed at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，舟山置定海縣，以舊縣改置鎮海。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, Dinghai County was established on Zhoushan, and the former county was reorganized as Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 36 (1697), Dinghai County was established on Zhoushan, and the former county seat was reorganized as Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，增置溫台玉環廳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, the Wen-Tai Yuhuan subprefecture was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 (1728), the Wen-Tai Yuhuan subprefecture was added.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，升定海為直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, Dinghai was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 (1841), Dinghai was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，升海寧縣為州，降安吉州為縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, Haining County was promoted to a prefecture, and Anji Prefecture was demoted to a county.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 (1773), Haining County was promoted to a prefecture, and Anji Prefecture was demoted to a county.

sentences.zh: 領府十一，直隸廳一，州一，廳一，縣七十五。

translations.idiomatic: The province comprised eleven prefectures, one directly administered subprefecture, one autonomous prefecture, one subprefecture, and seventy-five counties.

translations.idiomatic: To the north, Shengtang Stream passed through three stone sluice gates that regulated seasonal discharge.

sentences.zh: 其東涌金閘，導之入城，曰城河。

translations.literal: To its east, the Yongjin Sluice channeled water into the city, called the City River.
translations.idiomatic: To the east, the Yongjin Sluice channeled water into the city as the City River.

sentences.zh: 浙江，古淛河，東南自富陽入。

translations.idiomatic: The Zhe River, the ancient Zhe River, entered from the southeast at Fuyang.

translations.idiomatic: The Zhe River entered from the southwest through Xiaoshan and Qiantang and flowed northeast to the sea.

translations.idiomatic: The stone seawall extended from the first bastion at Wulong Temple in Qiantang to the twelfth bastion at Qijing Village, administered by the western defense sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 又東至翁家埠十七堡，中防同知治。

translations.literal: Farther east to Wengjiabu, seventeenth bastion, under the central defense sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east to the seventeenth bastion at Wengjiabu, administered by the central defense sub-prefect.

translations.idiomatic: The name was sometimes written with the alternate character "洩"; Xie Stream rose here.

translations.literal: To the west: Mount Bei.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood Mount Bei.

translations.literal: To the north: Tong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay Tong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 富春江，浙江上流，西南自桐廬入，納浦江。

translations.literal: The Fuchun River, upper reaches of the Zhe River, entered from the southwest at Tonglu and received the Pujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuchun River—the upper Zhe—entered from the southwest at Tonglu and received the Pujiang.

sentences.zh: 湖洑水即壺源江，右合剡浦，左納莧浦，自天目山伏流，入縣西北始出山。

translations.literal: Hufu Water is the Huyuan River; on the right it joined Yanpu, on the left received Xianpu; it flowed underground from Mount Tianmu and emerged in the northwest of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Hufu Water is the Huyuan River, which joined Yanpu on the right and received Xianpu on the left; it ran underground from Mount Tianmu and first surfaced in the county's northwest.

sentences.zh: 錯出復入，流為白洋溪，逕城南，合安吳川，抵漁山埠，北入錢塘，南入蕭山。

translations.literal: Emerging and re-entering in turn, it flowed as Baiyang Stream, passed south of the city, joined the Anwu River, reached Yushan Bank, and entered north into Qiantang and south into Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Breaking out and sinking back underground in turn, it became Baiyang Stream, passed south of the city wall, joined the Anwu River, and reached Yushan Bank, where it flowed north into Qiantang and south into Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 城河即慶春河，起觀山訖莧浦。

translations.literal: The City River is the Qingchun River, running from Mount Guan to Xianpu.
translations.idiomatic: The City River was the Qingchun River, running from Mount Guan to Xianpu.

translations.literal: Two sluice gates.
translations.idiomatic: There were two sluice gates.

sentences.zh: 有漁山、靈橋、場口、湯家、洋波場五鎮。

translations.literal: There were the five market towns of Yushan, Lingqiao, Changkou, Tangjia, and Yangbochang.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Yushan, Lingqiao, Changkou, Tangjia, and Yangbochang.

translations.literal: Huijiang Post.
translations.idiomatic: Huijiang Post was stationed here.

translations.literal: Yuhang: populous, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhang: populous and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Seventy li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seventy li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Mount Youquan.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood Mount Youquan.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Mount Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood Mount Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 北：獨松嶺，並百丈、幽嶺為三關。

translations.literal: To the north: Dusong Ridge, which together with Baizhang and You formed the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay Dusong Ridge, which with Baizhang and You ridges formed the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 南苕溪、中苕溪西自臨安分入而合，會北苕溪，為瓶窯大河。

translations.literal: The Southern and Middle Tiao Creeks entered separately from the west at Lin'an and joined, meeting the Northern Tiao Creek to form the Pingyao Great River.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern and Middle Tiao Creeks entered separately from Lin'an on the west and merged, joining the Northern Tiao Creek to form the Pingyao Great River.

sentences.zh: 又一支出武康界孔井山入焉。

translations.literal: Another branch entered from Kongjing Mountain at the Wukang border.
translations.idiomatic: Another branch entered from Kongjing Mountain on the Wukang border.

sentences.zh: 南苕性悍，逼臨城東，廝二瀽以引之，自滾壩泄流為餘杭塘河。

translations.literal: The Southern Tiao was fierce in nature and pressed on the east of the city; two diversion sluices were built to channel it, and from the Rolling Dam it discharged as the Yuhang Embankment River.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tiao ran fierce and pressed against the city's east; two diversion sluices were built to channel it, and from the Rolling Dam it discharged as the Yuhang Embankment River.

sentences.zh: 其南南湖，北流為黃母港，會苕溪，分上湖、下湖。

translations.literal: South of it was South Lake; flowing north it became Huangmu Harbor, joined the Tiao Creek, and divided into Upper and Lower Lakes.
translations.idiomatic: South of it lay South Lake; flowing north it became Huangmu Harbor, joined the Tiao Creek, and split into Upper and Lower Lakes.

translations.literal: Three market towns: Shuangxi, Shilai, and Xianlin.
translations.idiomatic: There were three market towns: Shuangxi, Shilai, and Xianlin.

translations.literal: Lin'an: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an: administratively simple.

translations.literal: One hundred li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the southwest: Mount Lin'an, from which the county took its name.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest stood Mount Lin'an, which gave the county its name.

translations.literal: To the west: Maple Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay Maple Ridge.

sentences.zh: 天目山，即山海經浮玉之山，苕水出其陰，合董、平、鵠三溪。

translations.literal: Mount Tianmu, that is the Floating Jade Mountain of the Classic of Mountains and Seas; Tiao Water issued from its northern slope and joined the three streams of Dong, Ping, and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tianmu—the Floating Jade Mountain of the Classic of Mountains and Seas—sent forth Tiao Water from its northern slope, which joined the Dong, Ping, and Hu streams.

sentences.zh: 又東南，右合潘溪，左合馬跑泉，側城北而東，錦溪合南溪入焉。

translations.literal: Flowing southeast, on the right it joined Pan Stream, on the left joined Mapao Spring; passing the city's north and running east, Jin Stream joined South Stream to enter it.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing southeast, it joined Pan Stream on the right and Mapao Spring on the left; skirting the north of the city and running east, Jin Stream and South Stream merged into it.

sentences.zh: 又東為南苕溪，西北為中苕溪。

translations.literal: Flowing east it became the Southern Tiao Creek; flowing northwest it became the Middle Tiao Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing east it became the Southern Tiao Creek; flowing northwest, the Middle Tiao Creek.

sentences.zh: 松溪出南黃嶺，其西婁塘，當苕之：衝，乾隆五年圮。

translations.literal: Song Stream emerged from South Huang Ridge; to its west, Loutang, at the Tiao River—strategically important; collapsed in the fifth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Stream rose at South Huang Ridge; west of it, Loutang occupied a strategically important position on the Tiao River but collapsed in Qianlong 5.

sentences.zh: 有青山、亭川、板橋、化龍、橫坂、三口、鶴山七鎮。

translations.literal: There were the seven market towns of Qingshan, Tingchuan, Banqiao, Hualong, Hengban, Sankou, and Heshan.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Qingshan, Tingchuan, Banqiao, Hualong, Hengban, Sankou, and Heshan.

translations.literal: Qingshan was near the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshan lay close to the county seat.

sentences.zh: 公、姥二山夾鎖苕源，最險要。

translations.literal: The two mountains of Gong and Lao pinched and guarded the source of the Tiao, the most perilous point.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Gong and Mount Lao pinched the source of the Tiao between them—the most perilous point in the region.

translations.literal: Yuqian: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqian: administratively simple.

translations.literal: One hundred seventy li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred seventy li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the east: Mount Shizhu.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood Mount Shizhu.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Longxiang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lay Longxiang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 西：天目，上有兩池，若左右目。

translations.literal: To the west: Tianmu, with two pools on its summit like left and right eyes.
translations.idiomatic: To the west rose Tianmu, with two pools on its summit like a pair of eyes.

sentences.zh: 左屬臨安曰東溪，右曰西溪，出尖頂，合流，逕白鶴橋雙溪口，合虞溪為浮溪。

translations.literal: That on the left belonging to Lin'an was called East Creek, that on the right West Creek; emerging from the pointed summit they joined, passed Shuangxikou at Baihe Bridge, and joined Yu Stream to form Fu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: The stream on the left, belonging to Lin'an, was called East Creek and that on the right West Creek; issuing from the pointed summit they merged, passed Shuangxikou at Baihe Bridge, and joining Yu Stream became Fu Stream.

sentences.zh: 至寮車橋，左合藻溪，右合交溪。

translations.literal: At Liaoche Bridge, on the left it joined Zao Stream, on the right joined Jiao Stream.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoche Bridge it joined Zao Stream on the left and Jiao Stream on the right.

sentences.zh: 紫溪西南自昌化入合之。

translations.literal: The Zi Stream entered from the southwest at Changhua and joined it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zi Stream entered from Changhua on the southwest and merged with it.

translations.literal: Its upper reach was Liu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Its upper reach was Liu Stream.

sentences.zh: 有千秋、白沙、桐嶺、豪千、孔夫諸關。

translations.literal: There were the passes of Qianqiu, Baisha, Tongling, Haoqian, and Kongfu.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the passes of Qianqiu, Baisha, Tongling, Haoqian, and Kongfu.

translations.literal: Xincheng: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng: administratively simple.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the west: Mount Dalei.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stood Mount Dalei.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Qingniu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest lay Qingniu Ridge.

translations.literal: Both are foothills of Tianmu.
translations.idiomatic: Both were foothills of Tianmu.

translations.literal: To the south: Baizhang Ridge, on the border with Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Baizhang Ridge, on the border with Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 葛溪出，合武源、里仁二水，出大源橋，右合菖溪，左納槎溪，上承分水廣陵溪為三溪口，逕練頭庄為練頭溪，合松溪為雙港口，曰鼉江。

translations.literal: Ge Stream emerged, joined the two waters of Wuyuan and Liren, issued at Dayuan Bridge, on the right joined Chang Stream, on the left received Cha Stream; its upper course received the Fenshui Guangling Stream as Sanxikou, passed Liantouzhuang as Liantou Stream, joined Song Stream to form Shuanggangkou, called Tuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Stream rose and joined the Wuyuan and Liren rivers, issued at Dayuan Bridge, joined Chang Stream on the right and received Cha Stream on the left; its upper course took in the Fenshui Guangling Stream at Sanxikou, passed Liantouzhuang as Liantou Stream, and joining Song Stream at Shuanggangkou became the Tuo River.

translations.literal: To the north was Tashan Dam.
translations.idiomatic: Tashan Dam lay to the north.

translations.literal: There was Dong'an Market Town.
translations.idiomatic: The county had Dong'an Market Town.

translations.literal: Changhua: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Changhua: administratively simple.

translations.literal: Two hundred ten li west of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay two hundred ten li west of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the southwest: Mount Fuquan; to its east, Lu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest stood Mount Fuquan; east of it lay Lu Ridge.

translations.literal: To the south: Yang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Yang Ridge.

translations.literal: To the west: Yu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the west lay Yu Ridge.

translations.literal: To the north: Qiao Ridge and Huanghua Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay Qiao Ridge and Huanghua Ridge.

translations.literal: On all of them passes were established.
translations.idiomatic: Passes were established on all of them.

sentences.zh: 又馬頭嶺，上溪出，合高溪、仁里溪，東流為無他溪。

translations.literal: Again at Matou Ridge, Shang Stream emerged, joined Gao Stream and Renli Stream, and flowing east became Wuta Stream.
translations.idiomatic: At Matou Ridge, Shang Stream rose, joined Gao Stream and Renli Stream, and flowing east became Wuta Stream.

sentences.zh: 合雲溪，右納頰口溪，逕晚山下為西晚溪，逕城南為雙溪。

translations.literal: It joined Yun Stream, received Jiakou Stream on the right, passed beneath Mount Wan as Xiwan Stream, and passing south of the city became Shuang Stream.
translations.idiomatic: It joined Yun Stream, received Jiakou Stream on the right, passed beneath Mount Wan as Xiwan Stream, and skirting the south of the city became Shuang Stream.

translations.literal: Flowing south again it became Xiayuan Stream and San Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south it became Xiayuan Stream and San Stream.

sentences.zh: 伽溪南峽川，上博溪東南納分水青坑溪、覽溪，西南承蕭、浦二水，以達柳溪。

translations.literal: Qie Stream at Nanxia River; Shangbo Stream on the southeast received the Fenshui Qingkeng Stream and Lan Stream; on the southwest it received the Xiao and Pu two waters to reach Liu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Qie Stream ran at Nanxia River; Shangbo Stream on the southeast received the Fenshui Qingkeng and Lan streams, and on the southwest took in the Xiao and Pu rivers to reach Liu Stream.

sentences.zh: 其中柯相公潭，與於潛為界水。

translations.literal: Within it was Ke Xianggong Pool, a boundary water with Yuqian.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Xianggong Pool lay within it, forming a boundary river with Yuqian.

translations.literal: There were the three market towns of Shouyi, Jiakou, and Keqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Shouyi, Jiakou, and Keqiao.

translations.literal: Jiaxing Prefecture: strategically important, populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing Prefecture: strategically important, populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.

translations.literal: The brigade-general was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: A brigade-general was stationed here.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十五年裁所，並海寧衛為嘉興府。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Qianlong the office was abolished, and Haining Guard was merged into Jiaxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 15 the office was abolished and Haining Guard was merged into Jiaxing Prefecture.

translations.literal: One hundred eighty li southwest from the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred eighty li southwest of the provincial seat.

translations.literal: Its width was one hundred fifty li, its length one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured one hundred fifty li from east to west and one hundred li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十度五十二分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude thirty degrees fifty-two minutes.
translations.idiomatic: North polar altitude was 30°52′.

translations.literal: East of the capital four degrees three minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Longitude east of the capital was 4°03′.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed seven counties.

translations.literal: Jiaxing: strategically important, populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing: strategically important, populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 府境之水二派，曰武林、天目，而天目派由石門、秀水入運，則合武林為一。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture the waters divided into two branches, called Wulin and Tianmu; the Tianmu branch entered the Grand Canal through Shimen and Xiushui, merging with Wulin into one.
translations.idiomatic: Waters within the prefecture fell into two branches, the Wulin and Tianmu lines; the Tianmu branch entered the Grand Canal via Shimen and Xiushui, merging with the Wulin line into one.

sentences.zh: 長水塘南自桐鄉、海鹽界入，合練浦塘。

translations.literal: Changshui Embankment entered from the south at the Tongxiang and Haiyan border and joined Lianpu Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Changshui Embankment entered from the Tongxiang–Haiyan border on the south and joined Lianpu Embankment.

sentences.zh: 海鹽塘東南自其縣入，並匯於南湖，一名鴛鴦湖，東南接滮湖。

translations.literal: Haiyan Embankment entered from the southeast at that county, and all converged at South Lake, also called Mandarin Duck Lake, which connected on the southeast with Biao Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyan Embankment entered from the southeast at Haiyan County, and all converged at South Lake—also called Mandarin Duck Lake—which on the southeast connected with Biao Lake.

sentences.zh: 六里涇承南湖水，歧為二，一魏塘，一漢塘。

translations.literal: Liuli Creek received South Lake water and divided in two: one Wei Embankment, one Han Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Liuli Creek took water from South Lake and split in two—the Wei Embankment and the Han Embankment.

sentences.zh: 合王廟、空廟、眾歡諸塘，左出枝津為伍子塘。

translations.literal: Joining the embankments of Wang Temple, Empty Temple, Zhonghuan, and others, on the left a branch channel became Wuzi Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Joining the Wang Temple, Empty Temple, Zhonghuan, and other embankments, a branch on the left became Wuzi Embankment.

sentences.zh: 有王店、新豐、鍾埭、新禮四鎮。

translations.literal: There were the four market towns of Wangdian, Xinfeng, Zhongdai, and Xinli.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Wangdian, Xinfeng, Zhongdai, and Xinli.

translations.literal: Wangdian and Xinfeng had garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts were stationed at Wangdian and Xinfeng.

translations.literal: At Xishui Post there was an assistant official.
translations.idiomatic: An assistant official was stationed at Xishui Post.

translations.literal: There was a railway.
translations.idiomatic: A railway ran through the county.

translations.literal: Xiushui: strategically important, populous, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushui: strategically important, populous, and difficult to govern.

sentences.zh: 明宣德四年析嘉興置，同附郭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande of the Ming it was separated from Jiaxing and established, attached to the prefectural seat as an outer county.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Ming Xuande 4 by division from Jiaxing, it was attached to the prefectural seat as an outer county.

sentences.zh: 西南：運河自桐鄉入，合石人涇，左出枝津為新塍南塘，側城西南注南湖。

translations.literal: To the southwest: the Grand Canal entered from Tongxiang, joined Shiren Creek, on the left a branch channel became Xincheng South Embankment, and passing the southwest of the city discharged into South Lake.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest the Grand Canal entered from Tongxiang, joined Shiren Creek, sent a branch on the left as Xincheng South Embankment, and passing southwest of the city discharged into South Lake.

sentences.zh: 新塍塘西北自江蘇震澤入，納新塍北塘，與南塘合，逕北麗橋。

translations.literal: Xincheng Embankment entered from the northwest at Zhenze in Jiangsu, received Xincheng North Embankment, joined with South Embankment, and passed Beili Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng Embankment entered from Zhenze in Jiangsu on the northwest, received Xincheng North Embankment, merged with South Embankment, and passed Beili Bridge.

sentences.zh: 長水、海鹽二塘東南自嘉興注之，是為秀水，縣以是名。

translations.literal: The Changshui and Haiyan embankments entered from the southeast at Jiaxing and discharged into it; this was Xiushui, from which the county took its name.
translations.idiomatic: The Changshui and Haiyan embankments entered from Jiaxing on the southeast and discharged here—this was Xiushui, which gave the county its name.

sentences.zh: 東北流，右出枝津北流，瀦為姚涇、楊舍、上馬諸港，分趨南官、北官、連四、梅家、陸家諸盪，入江蘇吳江。

translations.literal: Flowing northeast, on the right a branch channel flowed north and backed up into the harbors of Yaojing, Yangshe, Shangma, and others, dividing toward the marshes of Nanguan, Beiguan, Liansi, Meijia, Lujia, and others, and entering Wujiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing northeast, a branch on the right ran north and backed up into the harbors of Yaojing, Yangshe, Shangma, and others, spreading toward the marshes of Nanguan, Beiguan, Liansi, Meijia, Lujia, and the like before entering Wujiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 魏塘，東自嘉興入，入嘉善。

translations.literal: Wei Embankment entered from the east at Jiaxing and entered Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Embankment entered from Jiaxing on the east and flowed into Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 爛溪，西北自桐鄉入，入震澤、吳江為界水。

translations.literal: Lan Stream entered from the northwest at Tongxiang and entered Zhenze and Wujiang as a boundary river.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Stream entered from Tongxiang on the northwest and flowed into Zhenze and Wujiang as a boundary river.

translations.literal: At Wangjiangjing, the sub-prefect was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The sub-prefect was stationed at Wangjiangjing.

sentences.zh: 舊設同知及東西兩塘協辦同知，並裁。

translations.literal: Formerly sub-prefects and cooperative sub-prefects for the eastern and western embankments were established; all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-prefects and cooperative sub-prefects for the eastern and western embankments had formerly been established; all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 濮院鎮、新塍、九里匯有汛。

translations.literal: At Puyuan Market Town, Xincheng, and Jiuli Hui there were garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts were stationed at Puyuan Market Town, Xincheng, and Jiuli Hui.

translations.literal: Two market towns: Xincheng and Lumen.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Xincheng and Lumen.

translations.literal: Jiashan: populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashan: populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Thirty li northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay thirty li northeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Mount Ping.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood Mount Ping.

sentences.zh: 魏塘自秀水入，會東郭湖塘，貫西城壕，出東門流為楓涇塘，入江蘇婁縣。

translations.literal: Wei Embankment entered from Xiushui, joined East Outer Lake Embankment, passed through the west city moat, issued from the east gate and flowed as Fengjing Embankment, entering Lou County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Embankment entered from Xiushui, joined East Outer Lake Embankment, ran through the west city moat, left the east gate as Fengjing Embankment, and entered Lou County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 伍子塘南自嘉興入，貫南城壕，出北門入祥符盪。

translations.literal: Wuzi Embankment entered from the south at Jiaxing, passed through the south city moat, issued from the north gate, and entered Xiangfu Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi Embankment entered from Jiaxing on the south, ran through the south city moat, left the north gate, and entered Xiangfu Marsh.

sentences.zh: 其北沈家、白魚、上白諸盪，西北烏盆潭、木斜湖、吳家漾，併入江蘇青浦。

translations.literal: To its north were the marshes of Shenjia, Baiyu, Shangbai, and others; to the northwest Wupen Pool, Muxie Lake, and Wujia Yang—all entered Qingpu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: North of it lay the marshes of Shenjia, Baiyu, Shangbai, and the like; to the northwest were Wupen Pool, Muxie Lake, and Wujia Yang, all discharging into Qingpu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 西北：汾湖潀流匯處，播為南北許盪、南北夏墓盪，入吳江。

translations.literal: To the northwest: where the rushing waters of Fen Lake gathered, they spread into South and North Xu Marshes and South and North Xiamu Marshes, and entered Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest, where Fen Lake's rushing waters converged, they spread into the South and North Xu and South and North Xiamu marshes before entering Wujiang.

translations.literal: At Xietang Market Town, the assistant magistrate was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant magistrate was stationed at Xietang Market Town.

translations.literal: At Fengjing Market Town, the registrar was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar was stationed at Fengjing Market Town.

translations.literal: Tianningzhuang Market Town had a garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison post was stationed at Tianningzhuang Market Town.

translations.literal: Three market towns: Wei Embankment, Taozhuang, and Ganjia Kiln.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Wei Embankment, Taozhuang, and Ganjia Kiln.

translations.literal: Haiyan: populous, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyan: populous and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Qinzhu.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Qinzhu.

translations.literal: To the southeast: White Pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood White Pagoda.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Mount Du.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood Mount Du.

sentences.zh: 海，東北自平湖入，逕縣城，又南至澉浦。

translations.literal: The sea entered from the northeast at Pinghu, passed the county seat, and continued south to Ganpu.
translations.idiomatic: The sea entered from Pinghu on the northeast, passed the county seat, and continued south to Ganpu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年設水師都司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang a naval garrison company commander was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 24 a naval garrison company commander was established.

sentences.zh: 其西長牆山，橫截海灣，建砲臺。

translations.literal: To its west, Mount Changqiang blocked the bay crosswise, and a fort was built.
translations.idiomatic: West of it, Mount Changqiang spanned the bay, where a fort was built.

sentences.zh: 捍海石塘，西南接海寧，東北亙平湖。

translations.literal: The seawall stone embankment joined Haining to the southwest and extended to Pinghu in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: The stone seawall linked Haining on the southwest with Pinghu on the northeast.

sentences.zh: 秦駐塢水出秦駐山，歧為三，通曰秦溪，縱橫數十里，貫以招寶、烏坵兩塘。

translations.literal: Qinzhu Dock water issued from Mount Qinzhu, divided into three branches, collectively called Qin Stream; running dozens of li in all directions, it was crossed by the Zhaobao and Wuqiu embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhu Dock water rose at Mount Qinzhu, split into three branches known collectively as Qin Stream; stretching dozens of li in every direction, it was crossed by the Zhaobao and Wuqiu embankments.

sentences.zh: 招寶塘西南自海寧入，烏坵塘出長生橋合之，是為嘉興塘。

translations.literal: Zhaobao Embankment entered from the southwest at Haining; Wuqiu Embankment issued from Changsheng Bridge and joined it—this was Jiaxing Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaobao Embankment entered from Haining on the southwest; Wuqiu Embankment issued from Changsheng Bridge and merged with it to form Jiaxing Embankment.

sentences.zh: 又自□興城東海貫城壕出北門流為平湖塘。

translations.literal: Again from the east of Jiaxing city it passed through the city moat, issued from the north gate, and flowed as Pinghu Embankment.
translations.idiomatic: From east of Jiaxing city it also ran through the city moat, left the north gate as Pinghu Embankment.

sentences.zh: 長水塘亦自海寧入，緣西北界，錯出復入，入嘉興、桐鄉為界水。

translations.literal: Changshui Embankment also entered from Haining, followed the northwest boundary, alternately issuing and re-entering, and entered Jiaxing and Tongxiang as a boundary river.
translations.idiomatic: Changshui Embankment also entered from Haining, ran along the northwest boundary in and out, and served as a boundary river between Jiaxing and Tongxiang.

translations.literal: There were two salt-field offices, at Baolang and Haisha.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-field offices were stationed at Baolang and Haisha.

translations.literal: Two market towns: Haikou and Zhendang.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Haikou and Zhendang.

translations.literal: There was a garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: A garrison post was stationed here.

translations.literal: Shimen: strategically important, populous, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Shimen: strategically important, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Eighty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay eighty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: In the Ming it was Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming it was called Chongde.

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi the name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: It was renamed in Kangxi 1.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Mount Han.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood Mount Han.

sentences.zh: 運河，西南自德清入，納海寧下塘枝水。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal entered from the southwest at Deqing and received the Haining Lower Embankment branch water.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal entered from Deqing on the southwest and received the Haining Lower Embankment branch.

sentences.zh: 左枝為南界涇，入歸安，右納下塘河、長安塘，並自海寧南注之。

translations.literal: On the left a branch became Nan Boundary Creek, entering Gui'an; on the right it received Lower Embankment River and Chang'an Embankment, both entering from the south at Haining.
translations.idiomatic: A branch on the left became Nan Boundary Creek and entered Gui'an; on the right it took in Lower Embankment River and Chang'an Embankment, both entering from Haining on the south.

sentences.zh: 左枝為南沙渚塘，入海寧、桐鄉為界水，側城南而北，右出二枝津為中北沙渚塘，又北襟塘，左石人、瓜塔、沙木諸涇，折東環灣如帶，是為王灣。

translations.literal: On the left a branch became South Shazhu Embankment, entering Haining and Tongxiang as a boundary river, passing south of the city toward the north; on the right two branch channels became Central-North Shazhu Embankment, then further north Jin Embankment; on the left Shiren, Guata, and Shamu creeks turned east to encircle a bay like a belt—this was Wang Bay.
translations.idiomatic: A branch on the left became South Shazhu Embankment and served as a boundary river between Haining and Tongxiang, passing south of the city northward; on the right two branches formed Central-North Shazhu Embankment and then Jin Embankment farther north; Shiren, Guata, and Shamu creeks on the left turned east to loop a bay like a belt—this was Wang Bay.

sentences.zh: 其塘右諸涇、半截運河注塘，左半由含山入歸安。

translations.literal: On the right of the embankment various creeks and half of the Grand Canal discharged into the embankment; on the left half entered Gui'an through Mount Han.
translations.idiomatic: Creeks on the right of the embankment and half the Grand Canal fed the embankment; the left half entered Gui'an via Mount Han.

translations.literal: There was Yuxi Market Town.
translations.idiomatic: The county had Yuxi Market Town.

translations.literal: Zaolin Post.
translations.idiomatic: Zaolin Post was stationed here.

translations.literal: Pinghu: populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Pinghu: populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Fifty-four li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay fifty-four li southeast of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 東南：雅山，又苦竹山，水師戰艦泊焉。

translations.literal: To the southeast: Mount Ya; also Mount Kuzhu, where naval warships were moored.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood Mount Ya; also Mount Kuzhu, where naval warships were moored.

sentences.zh: 迤東羊、許二山，峭立海中，為江、浙分疆處，浙西第三門戶也。

translations.literal: Continuing east, Mounts Yang and Xu, standing steeply in the sea, marked the boundary between Jiangsu and Zhejiang—the third gateway of western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east, Mounts Yang and Xu rose steeply from the sea at the Jiangsu-Zhejiang boundary—the third gateway of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 海，東南自江蘇金山衛入，又西逕乍浦。

translations.literal: The sea entered from the southeast at Jinshan Guard in Jiangsu, then passed west through Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: The sea entered from Jinshan Guard in Jiangsu on the southeast and passed west through Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年設水師營，七年，移杭州副都統來駐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng a naval garrison was established; in the seventh year the deputy lieutenant-general of Hangzhou was moved to be stationed here.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 a naval garrison was established; in Yongzheng 7 the Hangzhou deputy lieutenant-general was relocated here.

sentences.zh: 道光三年移府海防同知並駐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang the prefectural coastal-defense sub-prefect was moved to be stationed here as well.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3 the prefectural coastal-defense sub-prefect was also relocated here.

sentences.zh: 東西兩海口，北接廣陳汛。

translations.literal: East and west sea mouths; to the north joined Guangchen garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: There were eastern and western sea mouths; to the north they connected with the Guangchen garrison post.

sentences.zh: 自此入澉浦達杭州，為錢塘江口北岸，西人名乍浦灣。

translations.literal: From here one entered Ganpu to reach Hangzhou; it was the north bank of the Qiantang River mouth, which Westerners called Zhapu Bay.
translations.idiomatic: From here one entered Ganpu to reach Hangzhou—the north bank of the Qiantang estuary, known to Westerners as Zhapu Bay.

sentences.zh: 漢塘西自嘉興入，分流注當湖。

translations.literal: Han Embankment entered from the west at Jiaxing, divided, and discharged into Dang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Han Embankment entered from Jiaxing on the west, divided, and discharged into Dang Lake.

sentences.zh: 右得平湖塘，西南自海鹽入合之。

translations.literal: On the right it received Pinghu Embankment, which entered from the southwest at Haiyan and joined it.
translations.idiomatic: On the right it received Pinghu Embankment entering from Haiyan on the southwest and merging with it.

sentences.zh: 左得乍浦塘，出東南前黃山，合何陳塘注之。

translations.literal: On the left it received Zhapu Embankment, which issued southeast from Front Yellow Hill, joined He-Chen Embankment, and discharged into it.
translations.idiomatic: On the left it received Zhapu Embankment from Front Yellow Hill on the southeast, merged with He-Chen Embankment, and fed in.

sentences.zh: 東北流，歧為二，分流復合，入泖湖，其口曰硃洞港。

translations.literal: Flowing northeast, it divided into two; the branches rejoined and entered Mao Lake; its mouth was called Zhudong Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing northeast it split in two, then reunited and entered Mao Lake at a mouth called Zhudong Harbor.

translations.literal: There was one garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: One garrison post was stationed here.

sentences.zh: 廣陳塘右出枝津為鹽船河，出放港為秦河，入泖湖，正渠併入之。

translations.literal: Guangchen Embankment on the right issued a branch channel as Salt-Boat River, issued at Fang Harbor as Qin River, entered Mao Lake, and the main channel all entered it as well.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen Embankment sent a branch on the right as Salt-Boat River and another at Fang Harbor as Qin River into Mao Lake, with the main channel entering as well.

sentences.zh: 鎮五：白門、廣陳、戶浦、新埭、青蓮寺。

translations.literal: Five market towns: Baimen, Guangchen, Hupu, Xindai, and Qingliansi.
translations.idiomatic: The county had five market towns: Baimen, Guangchen, Hupu, Xindai, and Qingliansi.

translations.literal: There was a Baishawan patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: A patrol office was stationed at Baishawan.

translations.literal: Two salt fields: Luli and Hengpu.
translations.idiomatic: There were two salt fields, at Luli and Hengpu.

sentences.zh: 天后宮、觀山麓、陳山嘴砲臺。

translations.literal: Tianhou Palace, Guanshan Foot, and Chenshanzui Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhou Palace, Guanshan Foot, and Chenshanzui Fort were located here.

translations.literal: Tongxiang: populous, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxiang: populous and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Fifty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay fifty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the east: Mount Shu.
translations.idiomatic: To the east stood Mount Shu.

translations.literal: To the south: Mount Wangjia.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood Mount Wangjia.

sentences.zh: 運河西南自石門入，枝津入震澤界為爛溪，正渠逕永新橋歧為三，南流注永新港，達石人涇，北流注五往涇入爛溪，東流入秀水。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal entered from the southwest at Shimen; branch channels entered the Zhenze boundary as Lan Stream; the main channel passed Yongxin Bridge and divided into three—a southern flow discharged into Yongxin Harbor, reaching Shiren Creek; a northern flow discharged into Wuwang Creek and entered Lan Stream; an eastern flow entered Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal entered from Shimen on the southwest; branches entered the Zhenze boundary as Lan Stream; the main channel passed Yongxin Bridge and split three ways—south into Yongxin Harbor to Shiren Creek, north into Wuwang Creek and Lan Stream, and east into Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 石人涇亦自石門入，合瓜塔涇及北沙渚塘，逕屠甸，復合沙木涇。

translations.literal: Shiren Creek also entered from Shimen, joined Guata Creek and North Shazhu Embankment, passed Tudian, and again joined Shamu Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Shiren Creek also entered from Shimen, merged with Guata Creek and North Shazhu Embankment, passed Tudian, and joined Shamu Creek again.

sentences.zh: 南沙渚塘亦自石門入，合中沙渚塘，入海寧。

translations.literal: South Shazhu Embankment also entered from Shimen, joined Central Shazhu Embankment, and entered Haining.
translations.idiomatic: South Shazhu Embankment also entered from Shimen, merged with Central Shazhu Embankment, and flowed into Haining.

sentences.zh: 長水塘自海寧、海鹽緣東南界入海鹽、嘉興為界水。

translations.literal: Changshui Embankment from Haining and Haiyan followed the southeast boundary and entered Haiyan and Jiaxing as a boundary river.
translations.idiomatic: Changshui Embankment from Haining and Haiyan ran along the southeast boundary as a boundary river between Haiyan and Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 鎮五：濮院、爐鎮、皁林、陳庄，又青墩巡司。

translations.literal: Five market towns: Puyuan, Luzhen, Zaolin, and Chenzhuang; also a Qingdun patrol office.
translations.idiomatic: The county had the market towns of Puyuan, Luzhen, Zaolin, and Chenzhuang, and a patrol office at Qingdun.

translations.literal: Huzhou Prefecture: populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou Prefecture: populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit.

translations.literal: In the Ming it governed one department and five counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming it governed one department and five counties.

translations.literal: The brigade-general and garrison thousand-commander were stationed.
translations.idiomatic: A brigade-general and garrison thousand-commander were stationed here.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，改安吉為縣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, Anji was changed to a county.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 Anji was converted to a county.

translations.literal: One hundred eighty li southeast from the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one hundred eighty li southeast of the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 廣百八十二里，袤百三十八里。

translations.literal: Its width was one hundred eighty-two li, its length one hundred thirty-eight li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured one hundred eighty-two li from east to west and one hundred thirty-eight li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十度五十二分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude thirty degrees fifty-two minutes.
translations.idiomatic: North polar altitude was 30°52′.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東三度二十七分。

translations.literal: East of the capital three degrees twenty-seven minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Longitude east of the capital was 3°27′.

translations.literal: It governed seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed seven counties.

translations.literal: Wucheng: populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng: populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the south: Mount Heng and Mount Jingai.
translations.idiomatic: To the south stood Mount Heng and Mount Jingai.

translations.literal: To the northwest: Mount Bian.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest stood Mount Bian.

sentences.zh: 太湖，東北八十里，古震澤，周五百里，匯上游諸水。

translations.literal: Tai Lake, eighty li to the northeast, the ancient Zhenze, circumference five hundred li, gathering all upstream waters.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Lake lay eighty li to the northeast—the ancient Zhenze, five hundred li in circumference, gathering waters from upstream.

sentences.zh: 大小雷山扼其東，西亙長興，北至小雷界吳江。

translations.literal: Great and Little Lei Mountains guarded its east; westward it extended to Changxing; northward to Little Lei it bordered Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Great and Little Lei Mountains guarded its east; it stretched west to Changxing and north to Little Lei, where it bordered Wujiang.

translations.literal: The Zhe source divided into Eastern and Western Tiao streams.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang headwaters divided into the Eastern and Western Tiao streams.

sentences.zh: 東苕溪東南自歸安入，合西塘河注碧浪湖。

translations.literal: Eastern Tiao Stream entered from the southeast at Gui'an, joined Xitang River, and discharged into Bilang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Tiao Stream entered from Gui'an on the southeast, merged with Xitang River, and discharged into Bilang Lake.

translations.literal: Shantang Stream also from that county discharged into it.
translations.idiomatic: Shantang Stream from the same county also discharged into it.

sentences.zh: 合妙喜港，左得呂山塘，西北自長興入合之。

translations.literal: Joining Miaoxi Harbor, on the left it received Lushan Embankment, which entered from the northwest at Changxing and joined it.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Miaoxi Harbor, it received Lushan Embankment on the left entering from Changxing on the northwest and merging with it.

sentences.zh: 左出枝津為北塘河，分瀦二十五漊港。

translations.literal: On the left a branch channel became North Embankment River, backing up into twenty-five harbor inlets.
translations.idiomatic: A branch on the left became North Embankment River, backing up into twenty-five harbor inlets.

sentences.zh: 西苕溪亦自長興入，合四安溪。

translations.literal: Western Tiao Stream also entered from Changxing and joined Si'an Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Western Tiao Stream also entered from Changxing and merged with Si'an Stream.

sentences.zh: 左出枝津小梅港及橫港，分瀦十一漊港。

translations.literal: On the left branch channels Xiaomei Harbor and Heng Harbor backed up into eleven harbor inlets.
translations.idiomatic: Branches on the left at Xiaomei Harbor and Heng Harbor backed up into eleven harbor inlets.

sentences.zh: 正渠與東苕合，是為江渚，匯合瀦大錢港入太湖，三十六漊港併入之。

translations.literal: The main channel joined Eastern Tiao to form Jiang Isle; gathering and backing up at Daqian Harbor it entered Tai Lake—all thirty-six harbor inlets entered it as well.
translations.idiomatic: The main channel merged with Eastern Tiao to form Jiang Isle; gathering at Daqian Harbor it entered Tai Lake, with all thirty-six harbor inlets discharging into it.

sentences.zh: 其東，運河自歸安入，合潯溪入震澤。

translations.literal: To its east, the Grand Canal entered from Gui'an, joined Xun Stream, and entered Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: To its east the Grand Canal entered from Gui'an, merged with Xun Stream, and entered Zhenze.

sentences.zh: 爛溪自歸安、桐鄉緣界，左出枝津為白米塘河，納歸安中塘河併入之。

translations.literal: Lan Stream followed the boundary from Gui'an and Tongxiang; on the left a branch channel became Baimi Embankment River, receiving Gui'an Central Embankment River and all entering it.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Stream ran along the Gui'an-Tongxiang boundary; a branch on the left became Baimi Embankment River, receiving Gui'an Central Embankment River and feeding in.

sentences.zh: 太湖營守備駐，同知駐烏鎮，通判駐南潯溪，並晟舍、大錢、馬要、圓通橋、小梅、青山、伍浦有汛。

translations.literal: The Tai Lake garrison commandant was stationed; the sub-prefect at Wuzhen, the sub-prefect at Nanxun Creek; and at Shenghe, Daqian, Mayao, Yuantong Bridge, Xiaomei, Qingshan, and Wupu there were garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Tai Lake garrison commandant was stationed here; sub-prefects were at Wuzhen and Nanxun Creek; and garrison posts were stationed at Shenghe, Daqian, Mayao, Yuantong Bridge, Xiaomei, Qingshan, and Wupu.

translations.literal: Two patrol offices: Nanxun and Daqian Lake Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: There were patrol offices at Nanxun and Daqian Lake Mouth.

translations.literal: Tiaoxi Post.
translations.idiomatic: Tiaoxi Post was stationed here.

translations.literal: Gui'an: populous, tax-exhausted, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Gui'an: populous, fiscally strained, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: To the southeast: Mount Changchao.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood Mount Changchao.

translations.literal: To the southwest: Mount Meifeng.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest stood Mount Meifeng.

translations.literal: To the northeast: Tai Lake.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast lay Tai Lake.

sentences.zh: 東苕溪，東南自德清入，左出枝津為吳興塘，納石門含山塘注錢山漾。

translations.literal: Eastern Tiao Stream entered from the southeast at Deqing; on the left a branch channel became Wuxing Embankment, receiving Shimen Mount Han Embankment and discharging into Qianshan Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Tiao Stream entered from Deqing on the southeast; a branch on the left became Wuxing Embankment, receiving Shimen Mount Han Embankment and discharging into Qianshan Yang.

sentences.zh: 西塘河，南自武康入，洛舍漾逾埭溪注之，與東苕合。

translations.literal: Xitang River entered from the south at Wukang; Luoshe Yang crossed Dai Creek and discharged into it, joining Eastern Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xitang River entered from Wukang on the south; Luoshe Yang crossed Dai Creek and fed in, merging with Eastern Tiao.

sentences.zh: 逕城南，呂山塘西自烏程注之，右出枝津為菜花涇，播為運河，歷月河為霅溪，抵臨湖水門。

translations.literal: Passing south of the city, Lushan Embankment discharged into it from Wucheng on the west; on the right a branch channel became Caihua Creek, spreading as the Grand Canal, passing Moon River as Zha Stream, reaching Linhu Water Gate.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city, Lushan Embankment fed in from Wucheng on the west; a branch on the right became Caihua Creek and spread as the Grand Canal, following Moon River as Zha Stream to Linhu Water Gate.

sentences.zh: 自錢山漾至此，與烏程為界水。

translations.literal: From Qianshan Yang to here, it was a boundary river with Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: From Qianshan Yang to this point it served as a boundary river with Wucheng.

translations.literal: At Shuangling Market Town, the garrison commandant was stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commandant was stationed at Shuangling Market Town.

translations.literal: The assistant magistrate was stationed at Shecungang Market Town;
translations.idiomatic: The assistant magistrate was stationed at Shecungang Market Town;

translations.literal: The registrar was stationed at Linghu Market Town.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar was stationed at Linghu Market Town.

translations.literal: At Hanshan and Shanlian as well there were garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison posts were also stationed at Hanshan and Shanlian.

translations.idiomatic: To the southeast stood Mount Fenghua, for which the county was named.

translations.literal: Also Mount Jieqi.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jieqi also stood here.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年法兵艦來犯砲臺，斃其將孤拔，遂遁。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu French warships attacked the fort; their general Courbet was killed, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 10 French warships attacked the fort; Admiral Courbet was killed, and the fleet withdrew.

sentences.zh: 海，東北自鄞入，逕湖頭渡關，又西逕塔山城、應家棚，東接楊村汛，又西為河泊所。

translations.literal: The sea entered from the northeast at Yin, passed Hutoudu Pass, then west passed Tashan City and Yingjiapeng, east connecting with Yangcun garrison post, and farther west was the river berth office.
translations.idiomatic: The sea entered from Yin on the northeast, passed Hutoudu Pass, then west through Tashan City and Yingjiapeng, connected east with the Yangcun garrison post, and farther west reached the river berth office.

translations.literal: At its mouth was Mount Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Xuan stood at its mouth.

sentences.zh: 又天門山，下即漢志天門水，南為江彭山，界象山、寧海。

translations.literal: Also Mount Tianmen; below it was the Tianmen Water of the Han Gazetteer; south was Mount Jiangpeng, bordering Xiangshan and Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tianmen also stood here; below it was the Tianmen Water recorded in the Han Gazetteer; to the south was Mount Jiangpeng, on the border with Xiangshan and Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 縣溪出西南大公隩，七十二曲，硃、白二溪逾趙河注之。

translations.literal: County Stream issued from the southwest at Dagong'ao with seventy-two bends; Zhu and Bai streams crossed Zhao River to feed it.
translations.idiomatic: County Stream rose in the southwest at Dagong'ao with seventy-two bends; the Zhu and Bai streams crossed Zhao River to join it.

sentences.zh: 抵璡琳碶，歧流為長它江，抵三江口。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinlin Sluice, it divided as Changta River and reached Sanjiang Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinlin Sluice it divided as Changta River and reached Sanjiang Mouth.

sentences.zh: 金溪出東金瓘山，逕白杜河來會。

translations.literal: Jin Stream issued from east at Mount Jinguan, passed Baidu River to join.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Stream rose east at Mount Jinguan and joined via Baidu River.

sentences.zh: 其西剡溪，出六詔嶺，合左溪，納西晦溪，是為奉化江。

translations.literal: To its west, Shan Stream issued at Liuzhao Ridge, joined Zuo Stream, received Xihui Stream, forming the Fenghua River.
translations.idiomatic: To its west, Shan Stream rose at Liuzhao Ridge, merged with Zuo Stream, received Xihui Stream, and formed the Fenghua River.

sentences.zh: 又東合長它江，迤東北會甬江。

translations.literal: Farther east it joined Changta River and extended northeast to meet the Yong River.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east it merged with Changta River and flowed northeast to meet the Yong River.

translations.literal: Tashan City Inspection Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Tashan City Inspection Office was stationed here.

translations.literal: Yingjiapeng Defense Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: A defense commandant was stationed at Yingjiapeng.

translations.literal: There was Jieqi Market Town.
translations.idiomatic: Jieqi Market Town was located here.

translations.literal: Lianshan Post.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshan Post was stationed here.

translations.literal: Xiangling, Donggong, Tongzhao, and other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Forts stood at Xiangling, Donggong, Tongzhao, and elsewhere.

translations.literal: Zhenhai: strategically important, populous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai: strategically important and populous.

translations.literal: Sixty li northeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay sixty li northeast of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 海，西北自慈谿入，東至澥浦，水師參將駐，為郡北要害。

translations.literal: The sea entered from the northwest at Cixi, extended east to Xiepu; a naval deputy commander was stationed; it was the key point of the north of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The sea entered from Cixi on the northwest and extended east to Xiepu, where a naval deputy commander was stationed; it was the chief strongpoint of the prefecture's north.

sentences.zh: 又東逕招寶山抵鉗口門。

translations.literal: Farther east it passed Mount Zhaobao to reach Qian Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east it passed Mount Zhaobao and reached Qian Mouth.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年英兵艦由此登岸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang British warships landed here.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 British warships landed here.

sentences.zh: 其東蛟門，西虎蹲，並稱天險。

translations.literal: To its east was Jiaomen; to the west Hurdun; together called heaven-sent peril.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaomen lay to its east and Hurdun to its west; together they were called a heaven-sent barrier.

translations.literal: Farther east was Chuanshan Guard, facing Huangqi Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east stood Chuanshan Guard, facing Huangqi Ocean.

translations.literal: Farther east was Qitou Cape, facing Qi Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east stood Qitou Cape, facing Qi Ocean.

sentences.zh: 頭長、跳嘴山扼其口，並為郡東要害。

translations.literal: Touzhang and Tiaozui Mountains guarded its mouth; together they were the key points of the east of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Touzhang and Tiaozui Mountains guarded its mouth; together they formed the chief strongpoints of the prefecture's east.

sentences.zh: 轉南至霩 所，南接昆亭汛。

translations.literal: Turning south to Guo Guard, south connecting with Kunting garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: It turned south to Guo Guard and connected south with the Kunting garrison post.

translations.literal: Extending south to Pushan Mountain, facing Shuangyu Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Extending south to Pushan Mountain, it faced Shuangyu Harbor.

translations.literal: Farther south to Huang Isle, bordering Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lay Huang Isle, on the border with Yin.

sentences.zh: 外洋各島，其著者，東北七姊妹山，東西霍山，迤東搗杵山。

translations.literal: Outer-sea islands, the notable ones: northeast Seven Sisters Mountains, east-west Huo Mountain, extending east Daozhu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Among the outer-sea islands, the notable ones were Seven Sisters Mountains to the northeast, east-west Huo Mountain, and Daozhu Mountain farther east.

sentences.zh: 東距金塘水道為大隩子港。

translations.literal: East across the Jintang channel was Da'aozi Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: East across the Jintang channel lay Da'aozi Harbor.

sentences.zh: 轉南有天隍山，東西二嶼，界象山。

translations.literal: Turning south was Mount Tianhuang; east and west twin isles, bordering Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Turning south stood Mount Tianhuang and east-west twin isles on the border with Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 涌江西南自鄞入，入海口為大浹江口，即古甬句，東自張家堰至此，與鄞為界水。

translations.literal: Yong River entered from the southwest at Yin; at the estuary was Daxie River mouth, the ancient Yong-Gou; from Zhangjiayan in the east to here it served as a boundary river with Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Yong River entered from Yin on the southwest; its estuary was Daxie River mouth, the ancient Yong-Gou; from Zhangjiayan in the east to here it served as a boundary river with Yin.

sentences.zh: 西北諸水瀦為鳳浦、沈窖、靈緒、白沙四湖，播為巨河。

translations.literal: Northwestern waters pooled into the four lakes of Fengpu, Shenjiao, Lingxu, and Baisha, spreading as great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern waters pooled in the four lakes of Fengpu, Shenjiao, Lingxu, and Baisha and spread out as great rivers.

sentences.zh: 夾江河西自鄞分甬江水，逾白沙，歷鷺林，入前大河。

translations.literal: Jiajiang River branched Yong River water from Yin on the west, passed Baisha, passed Lulin, and entered the front great river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajiang River split Yong River water from Yin on the west, passed Baisha and Lulin, and entered the front great river.

sentences.zh: 中大河上流後江自慈谿入，北流為西河。

translations.literal: The upper reach of the middle great river, the rear river from Cixi, flowed north as West River.
translations.idiomatic: The upper reach of the middle great river, the rear river from Cixi, flowed north as West River.

sentences.zh: 大閘河上流松浦亦自其縣入，歧為三：一抵澥浦入海，一流為西大河入浹江河，一逕箭港為後大河。

translations.literal: The upper reach of Dazha River, Songpu also from that county, divided in three: one reached Xiepu to enter the sea; one flowed as West Great River into Xiejiang River; one passed Jiankou as Rear Great River.
translations.idiomatic: The upper reach of Dazha River, with Songpu also entering from that county, split in three: one reached Xiepu and entered the sea; one became West Great River and entered Xiejiang River; one passed Jiankou as Rear Great River.

sentences.zh: 其中港貫前、後兩河，併入城河，出頭二閘入海。

translations.literal: Zhonggang Harbor passed through front and rear rivers, merged into the city river, and issued at Tou'er Sluice to enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggang Harbor ran through the front and rear rivers, merged into the city river, and left through Tou'er Sluice to enter the sea.

sentences.zh: 其東南上河注逕大碶巿，中河逕穿山碶，會蘆江河海。

translations.literal: Its southeast upper river discharged passing Daqi Market Town; middle river passed Chuanshan Sluice, meeting Lu River, river, and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Its southeast upper river passed Daqi Market Town; the middle river passed Chuanshan Sluice and met the Lu River, the main river, and the sea.

translations.literal: There were Zhuangshi and Chaibu market towns.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangshi and Chaibu market towns were located here.

sentences.zh: 定海關有管界、長山、穿山三巡司。

translations.literal: Dinghai Customs had three inspection offices: Guanjie, Changshan, and Chuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai Customs had inspection offices at Guanjie, Changshan, and Chuanshan.

translations.literal: Three stations: Longtou, Chuanshan, and Qingquan.
translations.idiomatic: There were three stations: Longtou, Chuanshan, and Qingquan.

sentences.zh: 有北城角、威遠、定遠、宏遠、平遠、綏遠、靖遠、鎮遠各砲臺。

translations.literal: There were Beichengjiao, Weiyuan, Dingyuan, Hongyuan, Pingyuan, Suiyuan, Jingyuan, and Zhenyuan forts.
translations.idiomatic: Forts stood at Beichengjiao, Weiyuan, Dingyuan, Hongyuan, Pingyuan, Suiyuan, Jingyuan, and Zhenyuan.

translations.literal: Xiangshan: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshan: administratively simple.

translations.literal: Two hundred seventy li southeast of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay two hundred seventy li southeast of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 海，西自奉化入，逕西周渡，虎山扼其口，南接泗州頭汛。

translations.literal: The sea entered from the west at Fenghua, passed Xizhou Ford; Mount Hushan guarded its mouth; south connecting with Sizhoutou garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: The sea entered from Fenghua on the west, passed Xizhou Ford; Mount Hushan guarded its mouth; and it connected south with the Sizhoutou garrison post.

sentences.zh: 逕東西塔嘴入，為陳山渡，接海口汛。

translations.literal: Passed Dongxitazui to enter as Chenshan Ford, connecting Haikou garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: It passed Dongxitazui as Chenshan Ford and connected with the Haikou garrison post.

sentences.zh: 又東逕前倉所，西接珠溪汛，東對牛鼻山。

translations.literal: Farther east passed Qiancang Guard, west connecting Zhuxi garrison post, east facing Mount Niubi.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east it passed Qiancang Guard, connected west with the Zhuxi garrison post, and faced Mount Niubi to the east.

sentences.zh: 其東北獵戶角，為南岸盡處。

translations.literal: Its northeast was Liehujiao, the end of the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Its northeast was Liehujiao, the southern bank's end point.

sentences.zh: 迤南逕爵溪城，青門、羊背諸山扼之，並為郡南要害。

translations.literal: Extending south passed Juexi City; Qingmen, Yangbei, and other mountains guarded it; together they were key points of the south of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Extending south it passed Juexi City; Qingmen, Yangbei, and other mountains guarded it; together they formed the chief strongpoints of the prefecture's south.

sentences.zh: 其南天目山，東即韭山列島。

translations.literal: South was Mount Tianmu; east were the Jiushan Archipelago.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tianmu lay to the south; the Jiushan Archipelago lay to the east.

sentences.zh: 又南至昌國，順治中裁衛，置水師營都司。

translations.literal: Farther south to Changguo; in Shunzhi the guard was abolished and a naval battalion colonel was established.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lay Changguo; during the Shunzhi reign the guard was abolished and a naval battalion colonel was posted.

sentences.zh: 又南至石浦，明為所，道光三年移府海防同知駐。

translations.literal: Farther south to Shipu; under the Ming it was a guard; in the third year of Daoguang the prefectural coastal defense sub-prefect was moved here.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lay Shipu; under the Ming it was a guard office; in Daoguang 3 the prefectural coastal defense sub-prefect was moved here.

sentences.zh: 南出為東門，與小銅礁對峙。

translations.literal: South issued as East Gate, facing Little Copper Reef.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it opened as East Gate, facing Little Copper Reef.

sentences.zh: 中為銅瓦門，道光二十二年英兵艦來犯，由此門入。

translations.literal: In the middle was Tongwa Gate; in the twenty-second year of Daoguang British warships attacked and entered through this gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle was Tongwa Gate; in Daoguang 22 British warships attacked and entered through this gate.

sentences.zh: 過此曰下灣門、金齒門，西為林門、珠門。

translations.literal: Beyond this were called Xiawan Gate and Jinchi Gate; west were Lin Gate and Zhu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this lay Xiawan Gate and Jinchi Gate; to the west were Lin Gate and Zhu Gate.

translations.literal: Farther south to Datian Island.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south lay Datian Island.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，派開墾委員駐此。

translations.literal: In early Guangxu, an opening-reclamation commissioner was posted here.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Guangxu reign an opening-reclamation commissioner was posted here.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年改為撫民廳，移府通判、左營游擊駐樊嶴，守備、千總駐龍泉、鶴浦兩塘。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong it was changed to a civilian pacification subprefecture; the prefectural sub-prefect and Left Battalion battalion commander were moved to Fan'ao; defense commandant and company commander at Longquan and Hepu embankments.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 it was reorganized as a civilian pacification subprefecture; the prefectural sub-prefect and Left Battalion battalion commander were moved to Fan'ao, with a defense commandant and company commander at the Longquan and Hepu embankments.

sentences.zh: 島北為石浦港，西即三門灣。

translations.literal: North of the island was Shipu Harbor; west was Sanmen Bay.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu Harbor lay north of the island; Sanmen Bay lay to the west.

translations.literal: Turning west to Taining Isle, bordering Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Turning west to Taining Isle, it bordered Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 東大河出王家嶴及旋井、飛鳳諸山，注會源碶。

translations.literal: East Great River issued from Wangjia'ao and Xuanjing, Feifeng, and other mountains, discharging at Huiyuan Sluice.
translations.idiomatic: East Great River rose at Wangjia'ao and at Xuanjing, Feifeng, and other mountains, and discharged at Huiyuan Sluice.

sentences.zh: 南大河出鳳躍山，自西水門接諸河，注朝宗碶。

translations.literal: South Great River issued from Fengyue Mountain, from West Water Gate received various rivers, discharging at Chaozong Sluice.
translations.idiomatic: South Great River rose at Fengyue Mountain, received various rivers at West Water Gate, and discharged at Chaozong Sluice.

sentences.zh: 西大河出郭家諸澗，注靈長碶，併入海。

translations.literal: West Great River issued from various ravines at Guojia, discharging at Lingchang Sluice, merging to enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: West Great River rose from various ravines at Guojia, discharged at Lingchang Sluice, and merged into the sea.

sentences.zh: 上洋三碶蓄三河水，防泄下洋，下洋永豐諸碶防泄入海。

translations.literal: Three sluices of Upper Reach stored the three river waters to prevent discharge to Lower Reach; Yongfeng and other sluices of Lower Reach prevented discharge to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Three sluices in the upper reach stored the three river waters to prevent discharge to the lower reach; Yongfeng and other sluices in the lower reach prevented discharge into the sea.

translations.literal: There were Nantian and Zhushan inspection offices.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection offices were stationed at Nantian and Zhushan.

translations.literal: Qian'aoling, Gaotang Mountain, and other forts.
translations.idiomatic: Forts stood at Qian'aoling, Gaotang Mountain, and elsewhere.

translations.literal: Nantian: administratively simple.
translations.idiomatic: Nantian: administratively simple.

translations.literal: Formerly subordinate to Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly been subordinate to Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年新置，治大佛頭山麓。

translations.literal: Newly established in the third year of Xuantong; seat at the foot of Mount Dafotou.
translations.idiomatic: It was newly established in Xuantong 3, with its seat at the foot of Mount Dafotou.

sentences.zh: 孤峙海中，東、南、西大洋，惟北距石浦較近，水程十有餘里。

translations.literal: Standing alone in the sea; east, south, and west open ocean; only to the north was it relatively close to Shipu, a water distance of more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: It stood alone in the sea with open ocean to the east, south, and west; only to the north was it relatively close to Shipu, a water distance of more than ten li.

translations.literal: Of the ten isles of the sea, this ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ten isles of the sea, it ranked first.

sentences.zh: 明湯和懼趙宋遺族苞□，擬廢象山、棄滃洲，遂徙南田居民。

translations.idiomatic: In the Ming, Tang He feared that Song remnant clans were harboring people (bao cang, text damaged), planned to abolish Xiangshan and abandon Wuzhou, and relocated Nantian's residents.

translations.literal: Later groups again entered to reclaim and boil salt.
translations.idiomatic: Later groups again entered to reclaim land and boil salt.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，巡撫帥承瀛奏謂「明與定海、玉環並封禁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, Governor Shuai Chengying memorialized saying: "Nantian was sealed off together with Dinghai and Yuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3, Governor Shuai Chengying memorialized: "Nantian was sealed off together with Dinghai and Yuhuan.

sentences.zh: 嗣定、玉展辟而南田獨否，以彼泥潮而此沙壚，匪船易留，故復徙之」。

translations.literal: Later Ding and Yu were opened but Nantian alone was not, because those had muddy tides while this had sandy shoals where bandit ships easily lingered, so residents were again relocated."
translations.idiomatic: Later Dinghai and Yuhuan were opened but Nantian alone was not, because those had muddy tides while this had sandy shoals where bandit ships easily lingered, so residents were again relocated."

sentences.zh: 大小共一百八嶴，南路四十九，北路五十九。

translations.literal: Large and small totaled one hundred eight inlets; southern route forty-nine, northern route fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Large and small inlets totaled one hundred eight; the southern route had forty-nine and the northern route fifty-nine.

translations.idiomatic: Dinghai Directly Administered Subprefecture: administratively simple.

translations.literal: Subordinate to Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit.

translations.literal: Regional commander and sub-prefect stationed.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander and sub-prefect were stationed here.

translations.literal: Ancient Gouzhang territory.
translations.idiomatic: It occupied the ancient territory of Gouzhang.

translations.literal: Under the Ming it was a guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming it was organized as a guard.

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi it was changed to a county.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 it was reorganized as a county.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年升直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang it was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 21 it was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.

translations.literal: Seven hundred sixty li west of the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven hundred sixty li west of the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 廣百四十里，袤八十三里。

translations.literal: One hundred forty li wide and eighty-three li long.
translations.idiomatic: It measured one hundred forty li across and eighty-three li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高二十九度五十九分。

translations.literal: North polar latitude twenty-nine degrees fifty-nine minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Its north polar latitude was twenty-nine degrees fifty-nine minutes.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東五度五十八分。

translations.literal: East of the capital by five degrees fifty-eight minutes.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five degrees fifty-eight minutes east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 舟山，古翁洲山，即定海山。

translations.literal: Zhoushan, ancient Wengzhou Mountain, that is Mount Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoushan, the ancient Wengzhou Mountain, was Mount Dinghai.

translations.literal: During Kangxi and Daoguang it fell to the British.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi and Daoguang reigns it fell to the British.

translations.literal: During Xianfeng it again fell to Britain and France.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign it again fell to Britain and France.

translations.literal: Outer islands of the bay towered ruggedly.
translations.idiomatic: Islands outside the bay rose ruggedly from the sea.

sentences.zh: 西洋螺角，東竟留角，對峙若門。

translations.literal: Xiyang Luojiao and Dongjing Liujiao faced each other like a gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyang Luojiao and Dongjing Liujiao faced each other like a gate.

sentences.zh: 洋螺南為螺頭山，西即大榭山，接象山港。

translations.literal: South of Yangluo was Luotou Mountain; west was Daxie Mountain, connecting with Xiangshan Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: South of Yangluo stood Luotou Mountain; to the west was Daxie Mountain, connecting with Xiangshan Harbor.

translations.literal: Islands north of the mouth formed perilous garrison posts of the subprefecture's south.
translations.idiomatic: Islands north of the mouth formed perilous garrison posts on the subprefecture's south.

sentences.zh: 又六橫山西對前倉嘴，牛鼻山扼其中。

translations.literal: Farther east, Liheng Mountain faced Qiancang Point; Mount Niubi guarded the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east, Liheng Mountain faced Qiancang Point, with Mount Niubi guarding the middle.

sentences.zh: 其東南為桃花山、登步山。

translations.literal: To its southeast were Taohua Mountain and Dengbu Mountain.
